title: Apparent collapse — faith seems only moral, below scientia
source_text: XXVIII. Unde corruere videtur certitudo illa summa, & ipsa scientiarum certitudine major quam Theologi fidei tribuunt. Si enim dogmatis credendis assentimur, quoniam illa Deus in verbo suo revelavit, Deum vero revelasse non persuademur vi alicujus demonstrationis, sed argumentis tantum moralibus, inde sequitur fidem ad illa tandem argumenta reduci, ac proinde fidei non competere nisi certitudinem moralem, & quae sit scientiarum certitudine inferior.
pass_a_gloss: Whence that highest certainty, and greater than the certainty of the sciences themselves, which the Theologians attribute to faith, seems to fall. For if we assent to dogmas to be believed because God has revealed them in His word, but we are not persuaded that God has revealed by the force of any demonstration, but only by moral arguments, it follows that faith is at last reduced to those arguments, and therefore that to faith belongs only moral certainty, and that which is inferior to the certainty of the sciences.
pass_b_english: Apparent ruin of faith’s claimed supra-scientia certainty.
Assent because God revealed — but ‘God revealed’ only morally argued.
Seems: faith reduces to moral certainty < scientiae.
